title: Case Report: A severe case of human parechovirus encephalitis in a neonate.
summary: Human parechovirus is a common pathogen causing respiratory and gastroenterological symptoms. Symptoms range from asymptomatic courses to rare encephalitis or sepsis-like symptoms. Studies regarding neurodevelopment after parechovirus encephalitis in infants are conflicting with indications of possible short or long term neurodevelopmental impairments. In this case report we describe an especially severe course of human parechovirus infection. A two-week-old infant presented with fever and developed seizures and apneic episodes after admission. summary: Neuro-Behçet disease (NBD) is a rare but potentially disabling manifestation of Behçet disease (BD). summary: We describe a case of a patient with multiple sclerosis (MS) stable on natalizumab who developed widespread gadolinium-enhancing lesions and clinical relapse seven and eight months after gamma knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for left cerebellar convexity meningioma. title: Macroscopic cerebral energy efficiency corresponds to neuron reorganization in awake and anesthetized mice.
summary: Non-invasive imaging of brain function and energy supply is crucial for diagnosing and treating brain disorders. Conventional imaging struggles to capture altered relationships between energy supply and demand caused by brain diseases. However, whether rPWR/rCST tracks individual changes and relate to neural activity remains unproven. title: A robust adversarial learning framework for EEG emotion recognition.
summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides an objective means of capturing neural patterns associated with emotion, but substantial inter-subject variability limits the ability of existing models to generalize to unseen subjects. We propose a robust adversarial domain generalization framework for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition. In the first stage, long short-term memory-based encoders are jointly trained to learn domain-invariant and domain-specific representations using reconstruction, emotion classification, and adversarial domain objectives. summary: Pain control in neonates is crucial as inadequate management may impair neuronal development. summary: Noninvasive neural decoding seeks to infer visual stimuli from brain recordings, such as EEG and MEG, thereby providing a computational approach for probing human visual information processing. title: A web modular AI interface for brain tumor MRI classification using deep learning models.
summary: In order to improve patient outcomes and treatment processes, early and precise diagnosis of brain tumors is crucial. Despite the strong performance shown by deep learning models in classifying brain tumors from MRI scans, integrating these models into user-friendly clinical workflows remains challenging. This study presents a web-based AI platform designed for brain tumor classification using MRI images. The platform enables users to upload MRI scans, apply standardized preprocessing, select between different deep learning models, and receive real-time predictions. summary: Although numerous neuroimaging studies have reported structural and functional abnormalities in migraine, results have remained heterogeneous. Emerging evidence suggests that neuropsychiatric symptoms may arise from dysfunction within distributed brain networks rather than isolated brain regions; however, migraine-related network abnormalities remain insufficiently explored. title: GNAI2 activating variants and MAGIS syndrome: long-term endocrine and growth outcome.
summary: Germline activating variants in the GNAI2 gene have recently been associated with MAGIS syndrome, characterized by midline malformations of the brain, anterior pituitary gland dysfunction, growth retardation, immunodysregulation, and skeletal defects. However, the full phenotypic spectrum, particularly regarding endocrine dysfunction, remains incompletely defined. title: Disease trajectory in cerebral amyloid angiopathy: a matter of time.
summary: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is a significant contributor to cerebrovascular disease, characterized by the deposition of amyloid-beta in the walls of cerebral small arteries and capillaries. This communication presents a detailed long-term follow-up of a 75-year-old female patient diagnosed with possible CAA in 2016, who demonstrated various clinical and neuroradiological manifestations over an 11-year period. title: Generalizable neural decoding for clinically scalable brain-computer interfaces.
summary: Brain-computer interfaces promise restored communication and movement, yet accuracy achieved under development rarely survives new sessions, users, tasks, or hardware. Generalization, not peak performance, determines clinical scalability. Here we examine generalizable neural decoding from development to deployment, organized by the domain held out at evaluation, target-data access, adaptation strategy, and the clinical conditions under which performance persists, identifying benchmarking standards, prospective validation, and hardware-algorithm co-design as prerequisites for durable benefit.

title: Incremental Prognostic Value of White Matter Hyperintensity Beyond Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System for Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events.
summary: This study aimed to assess the additional prognostic value of white matter hyperintensity (WMH) beyond Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease (CAD). This study included 1085 patients who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography and brain magnetic resonance imaging between November 2018 and December 2022. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves were used to evaluate the predictive values, and the C-statistic was employed to determine their discriminatory power. 170 (15.7%) patients experienced MACE during a median follow-up of 63.1 months.

title: Neural mechanisms underlying loss of functional independence after stroke: EEG evidence of impaired motor-to-sensory directed connectivity on the affected side.

This exploratory study investigates network reorganization patterns and their clinical relevance to motor function and daily independence using multimodal electroencephalography (EEG) connectivity analysis, including Coherence (COH), phase lag index (PLI), and Granger causality (GC). title: Diagnosis of a chiasmal lesion compressing optic chiasm in patients with severe retinal degeneration: a two-case report.

summary: Understanding the role of peer feedback, particularly rejection, is critical for adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD). summary: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading cause of disability worldwide, yet its neural basis and biomarkers remain elusive. title: Brain-State-Resolved Consistency of Corticospinal Responses to TMS.
summary: An important feature of motor-evoked potential (MEP) responses to transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) over the primary motor cortex (M1) is their substantial trial-to-trial variability. summary: To identify the timing and clinical risk factors associated with somatic growth faltering (GF) in very preterm infants (VPI, born < 32 weeks' gestation) and explore the relationship with longitudinal brain growth throughout the extrauterine second and third trimesters. title: Frustration Induction Alters Reward Prediction Error Encoding in Pediatric Irritability.

summary: Irritability is a prevalent, impairing, transdiagnostic affective symptom domain in youth associated with elevated risk for adverse outcomes. summary: Early caregiving may shape neonatal limbic circuit organization, yet whether microanalytically coded interaction quality relates to neonatal limbic-prefrontal connectivity is unknown. summary: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is hallmarked by pronounced inter-individual heterogeneity in brain function and clinical manifestations. title: Decoding individual differences in mental information from human brain responses predicted by deep neural networks.
summary: Brain decoding using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has high potential for evaluating unobservable mental information that varies across individuals in everyday situations. Although estimating individual differences in mental information using brain decoding could be effective for social applications, especially in neuromarketing, the physical constraints and high costs of fMRI limit the practical application in real-world settings. title: Do neuroimaging data have higher-order interactions?
summary: Recent advances in the physics of complex systems have motivated the study of higher-order structure in neuroimaging data, including functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), and magnetoencephalography (MEG). title: Coarse motor-state structure across paired preoperative fMRI and intraoperative ECoG in patients with brain tumors.
summary: Presurgical motor mapping in patients with tumors near eloquent motor cortex is commonly based on task-evoked activation maps, yet local BOLD responses may be difficult to interpret in lesion-affected tissue because of anatomical distortion, altered vascular coupling, and variability in task performance. summary: To characterise short- and long-term plastic changes in cortical and subcortical structures induced by ultra-long (five-day) monocular deprivation (MD), and to assess the extent and regional specificity of structural changes and their reversibility following the restoration of binocular vision. summary: To demonstrate intravenous ICG-assisted fluorescence mapping as an assistive tool for improving surgical precision and tissue differentiation during laparoscopic S2 root schwannoma excision. summary: The spatial organization of insular abnormalities across connectional-architecture-defined subregions in panic disorder (PD) remains unclear. title: Dynamic multi-scale topology learning and cross-modal graph fusion for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis.
summary: Multi-modal fusion methods have demonstrated potential in integrating complementary information from different data modalities. title: The Spectrum within the Spectrum: Neural Heterogeneity in Autism.
summary: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) encompasses diverse behavioral, cognitive, and neural profiles that vary widely across individuals. title: When emotion meets conflict: Additive but not synergistic effects in neural oscillatory activity.
summary: Cognitive control allows individuals to regulate their behavior in the face of conflicting or distracting information. summary: Conscious object recognition is a critical brain function, key to making sense of the plethora of visual inputs and guiding adaptive behavior. summary: Yeast extract (YE) is a widely used natural flavor enhancer whose taste and aroma quality govern its industrial value. title: Topography-specific white matter hyperintensities, hippocampal atrophy, and gait slowing as independent and interrelated correlates of late-life depression.

title: Structural brain correlates of symptom severity in stress-induced exhaustion.
summary: Exhaustion due to chronic stress, a hallmark feature of burnout, represents a substantial and growing public health burden, yet its structural brain correlates remain poorly understood. summary: The association between complete vascular ring (CVR) and prenatal brain development remains poorly characterized. summary: Whether emotional processing difficulties in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) stem from deficits in recognizing emotional stimuli or from limitations in flexibly reorganizing brain networks under increasing cognitive demands remains an open question. summary: Post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathy following oral and maxillofacial procedures may cause persistent neurosensory disturbances and neuropathic pain, yet the diagnostic performance of the available assessment methods remains uncertain. summary: The steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) is widely used for electroencephalography (EEG) based brain computer interfaces (BCIs).
